about: Every mutant was applied to the file as it is at base_commit, which the change that adds this record does not change. killer is the first test nextest reported failing (it stops at the first failure, with tests running in parallel, so another failing test may be reported first on another run). killer_at says where that test function exists: base, or this_commit for a test the change that adds this record adds. A test that exists at base may still kill only through cases that change adds to it: before_this_change gives the verdict at base where it differs. Each mutant that survived its filtered run at base was run again at base against every bridge test (the whole_set run) before it was called a survivor. Every survivor left at this_commit is listed in accepted_survivors with its reason: an equivalent one is marked equivalent, and one that is not says why it is not killed yet. A hand-written mutant's mutation id is the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its edits in order, each as its from text, a NUL byte, its to text and a NUL byte, in UTF-8. A tool mutant is named as cargo-mutants --list names it, by line and column. Every run was on base_commit, with the file and its test module byte for byte as there (or as this change leaves the test module, for survivors_again). A tool mutant that survived was run again in the whole_set and survivors_again runs as the same edit written as text, under the id named in its run's command.

runs.command: each mutant's edits applied as exact text, then cargo nextest run --locked -p bridge -E 'test(/stop|acknowledge|ack_tests|verify/)'

381:13 replace || with && in Server::rel.reason: equivalent: with && the check refuses when the generation changed, or when the sha256 changed and the batch no longer stops the company. With the generation unchanged no record of the batch was written since stop_held read it under the same lock as the stop it found. Whether a batch stops its company is decided by that batch's own records alone (ledger::invoice_stops), each of which moves its generation, and a batch's sha256 is fixed for its id. So with the generation unchanged both later conditions read false, and the check refuses exactly when it does at base

S50.reason: equivalent: the batch held after the read differs from the batch first read only by the records of it written in between, which change its status (persist_import_verification copies the line and sets its status). release_preview reads the company, company GUID, batch id and vouchers, never the status

S52.reason: equivalent: a batch's sha256 is fixed for its id. The build is the only writer of a batch line and mints a new batch id for each, and a verification's record copies the line with its sha256, so the batch held under the lock has the sha256 first read

S54.reason: equivalent: whether a batch stops its company is decided by that batch's own records alone (ledger::invoice_stops reads its batch lines and its dispatch, release and status records), and every one of them moves the batch's generation. stop_held read that generation under the same lock as the stop it found, so with the generation unchanged the batch still stops the company and this condition reads false

S56.reason: equivalent, unreachable: the stop_release record appended just before, under the same exclusive lock, names this batch, and ledger::invoice_stops leaves out a batch released since its latest posted_verified; nothing else is written before the journal is read again
